headline: Recommended a Route 127 road safety audit and removing Community Preservation Committee term limits.
summary: Speakers described ongoing safety problems on Rogers Street, and police reported 15 crashes with injuries and 90 with property damage over five years. The audit would be done by an outside engineering firm, and a state senator's office said it would seek state funding. Kelly Dolan said the Community Preservation Committee chair asked to remove the two-year term limit because it made recruiting members harder.
decisions: Recommended that the City Council approve a Road Safety Audit of Route 127 from East Main Street to Rogers Street, 2-0 with one absent.
Recommended that the City Council amend Code of Ordinances Sec. 2-534 to remove the two-term limit for Community Preservation Committee members, 2-0 with one absent.

This meeting was conducted in-person and remotely via ZOOM.
Agenda items were taken out of order, and the minutes reflect these changes.
The meeting was called to order at 6:00 p.m.
1. Memorandum from the Mayor regarding Route 127 road safety audit.
Summary of Discussion: Mayor Paul Lundberg stated that this matter had been brought forward after
consultation with Gorton’s Seafood regarding the safety of Rogers Street. He stated that due to the width of
the road, cars tended to speed on that section of road.
David Gazda, Gorton’s Seafood Director of CSR & ESH, stated that there had been ongoing safety issues
in the area and there had been several injuries and one fatality. He stated that there had been ongoing work
by the City Council to make the area safer, but a professional traffic study was needed. 
Interim Police Chief, Michael Gossom stated that at the request of CAO, Kelly Dolan he had looked back
at five years’ worth of traffic incidents in the area. He stated that during that five-year period there had been
112 medical emergencies, 15 vehicle accidents with injuries, 90 vehicle accidents with property damage, and
7 motor vehicle stops. He stated that this data was specifically for the area between Rogers Street at Flanagan
Square and the intersection of Rogers Street and Manuel F. Lewis Drive. He stated that the one fatality had
been investigated in conjunction with Mass. State Police and the Essex County District Attorney’s Office.
He stated that drivers tended to speed in that area, especially when coming downhill. 
Ted Costa, Deputy Director of Community Outreach for State Senator Bruce Tarr, stated that Rogers
Street was one of the two largest corridors in the City, and a road safety audit was important to conduct
considering the number of accidents. He stated he had shared with the administration previous road safety
audits, including one done in Rowley and one done in the City for Blackburn Circle. He stated that the State
Senator’s Office, along with State Representative Dru Tarr, would work to get the State to pay for the road
safety audit. He stated a road safety audit would be comprehensive and look at all factors that may impact the
safety of the area. 
CAO, Kelly Dolan stated that she supported the road safety audit.
O&A Committee November 16, 2026 Page 2 of 3
Ted Costa stated that a road safety audit would be conducted by an outside engineering firm, and would
include public outreach, studying traffic data, conducting a site visit, and then producing a detailed report
with short-term, mid-term, and long-term solutions. 
David Gazda stated that Gorton’s was a 24/7 operation and had roughly 300 employees that worked during
those hours. He stated that Gorton employees had to walk across Rogers Street multiple times a day during
all sorts of conditions. 
Councilor Grace stated that this matter had been in the works for over a year, beginning with dialog between
herself and the Traffic Commission. She stated that the intersection of Centennial Avenue, Washington Street,
and Grove Street should also have a safety audit conducted on it.  
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION:  On a motion by Councilor Grace, seconded by Councilor Nolan,
the Ordinances & Administration Committee voted 2 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 absent, to recommend that the
City Council approve the Mayor’s Office to conduct a Road Safety Audit of Route 127 from the intersection
of East Main Street, Route 128, and Bass Avenue in a west south westerly direction to the intersection of
Rogers Street, Washington Street, and Commercial Street. 
2. Memorandum from the General Counsel regarding a proposed amendment to Code of Ordinances
Sec. 2-534 concerning Community Preservation Committee term limits.
Summary of Discussion: Kelly Dolan stated that the chair of the Community Preservation Committee had
requested to remove the two-year term limit, as it was a hinderance for recruiting members. 
Councilor Nolan stated his support for the matter.
Councilor Grace stated her support for the matter.
